notes: Each retry is also a real request to Resend: with the provider failing, every save in the program re-sends to every opted-in member (no back-off), until the cap stops it. A refund in releaseDeliveries, or counting after a 2xx, would fix both.
title: Every failed urgent email spends one of the day's 60 immediate emails, so a Resend outage silently uses up the cap and later urgent alerts are held back with nothing ever delivered
steps: 1. Resend answers 503 (outage, bad key, 429). 2. Any mutation in a program with an urgent alert schedules sendImmediate; it claims (consume() adds 1 to rateLimits 'alerts:immediate'), the send fails, releaseDeliveries deletes the claim rows but does not give the email back. 3. Repeat 60 times in one UTC day (60 checks for one recipient, or 12 saves in a program with 5 opted-in members). 4. Resend recovers; run sendImmediate again.
expected: Only emails the provider accepted count against IMMEDIATE_EMAILS_PER_DAY (docs/alerts.md: 'Immediate emails stop at 60 a day'; the cap exists so the digest fits under Resend's 100 SENT emails). After recovery the pending urgent alert is emailed.
actual: sendImmediate returns {sent:0, capped:1}: the cap is spent by 60 failures, no urgent email goes out until 00:00 UTC. Members who get urgent emails but no digest (the maintenance-permission default) hear nothing until the next check after midnight UTC.
evidence: convex/urgentAlerts.ts:169 (reserveImmediateEmail inside claimDeliveries), :189-201 (releaseDeliveries deletes rows only), :402-408. Repro output: expected {sent:1,capped:0}, received {sent:0,capped:1}.
repro: repro/newb/zz-hunt-newb-urgent.test.ts (copy to convex/, then: npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-newb-urgent.test.ts -t NB-1)

notes: Rated High because the alert kind affected first is 'aircraft grounded', the reason the channel exists; the bell still shows it. Whether the stale row survives depends on chance: it is deleted only if the member gets some other NEW urgent alert on that channel while the first is cleared. The digest has the same flaw (NB-3), so a re-grounding can reach nobody by email at all. Related oddity from the same clean-up: grounded for {A} -> {A,B} -> {A} emails 'is grounded' a third time although nothing new happened, because the {A} row was deleted when {A,B} was claimed.
title: An urgent alert that cleared and later returns with the same key (an aircraft marked grounded again, a due date put back) is never emailed or pushed again, because the delivery claim is only forgotten when another new alert is claimed
steps: 1. Program with no other urgent alert. An administrator sets aircraft N206MA to Grounded in its profile: sendImmediate emails 'N206MA is grounded' (alertDeliveries row, channel immediate; the same happens on channel push). 2. The aircraft is returned to service: the alert clears. The check finds no urgent alert for the member, urgentRecipient returns undefined, so claimDeliveries (the only place that deletes stale rows) never runs. 3. Weeks later the aircraft is marked Grounded again. The key is the same (aircraft-grounded|<aircraft>|hash('profile:<aircraft>')).
expected: A new email and push for the new grounding (docs/alerts.md: 'the claim ... forgets claims for alerts that cleared'; ADR-0012 'No second send' is per state; brief: a new email when it recurs).
actual: sendImmediate returns sent:0, pushed:0: the stale row from the first grounding still marks the key as sent. The second grounding reaches nobody at once. The same holds for an inspection, AD, component or expiring date whose due point is changed and then put back (correction of a mistaken sign-off or date).
evidence: convex/urgentAlerts.ts:330-347 (emailed/pushed sets read every stored row, stale ones included; returns undefined before any clean-up), :160-163 (clean-up only inside claimDeliveries). Repro NB-2 output: expected sent 1, received sent 0. The push channel is confirmed by 'NB-2 (push)' in repro/newb/zz-hunt-newb-push.test.ts (expected pushed 1, received 0).
repro: repro/newb/zz-hunt-newb-urgent.test.ts (copy to convex/, then: npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-newb-urgent.test.ts -t NB-2)

title: A device keeps receiving a member's urgent alerts after they sign out or an administrator ends their sessions, and the next person on that device sees the switch already On

expected: No push to a device with no signed-in session for that account: sign-out unsubscribes the device (browser and server), and ending sessions or resetting the password removes the account's pushSubscriptions. For B the switch reflects whether B's account holds this device.

title: The digest job stops at the first Flight Program whose alert query throws, so every later program gets no digest and system administrators get no off-site backup warning that day
steps: 1. Two programs. The first holds one stored row that no longer parses (here an expiringItems payload from an older shape; any management, airworthiness, FAA monitor or expiring-date row has the same effect, and a system-wide expiring date is loaded into every program). 2. The 13:00 UTC cron runs alerts.sendDigests.

title: A single failed send (email or push) is never retried by itself: the urgent alert waits for the next change in that program or the next day's 13:10 UTC check
steps: 1. An aircraft is grounded at 14:00 UTC; sendImmediate runs. 2. Resend answers 503 once (or times out after 15 s); the claim is released and failed:1 is returned. 3. Nobody saves anything else in that program that day.
expected: The check schedules a later retry (with back-off) so an alert promised 'within a minute' is not held for up to 23 hours by one transient error.
actual: Nothing is scheduled: no second request is made in the following hour. The alert goes out only when some other mutation in the same program schedules a check, or at 13:10 UTC next day. The push channel behaves the same (convex/push.ts releases the claim and stops).
